BURSEVI:v6p77/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77/r2.claim: Those with light scales lack beliefs and deeds that have worth before God; they are unbelievers, as the verse about giving them no weight says.
BURSEVI:v6p77/r2.anchor: ومن لم يكن له من العقائد والأعمال ماله وزن وقدر عند الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v6p77/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77/r3.claim: They lose themselves by wasting the time needed to complete their potential; خسران means a shortfall in one's capital.
BURSEVI:v6p77/r3.anchor: ضيعوها بتضييع زمان استكمالها وأبطلوا استعدادها لنيل كمالها

BURSEVI:v6p77/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p77/r4.claim: Kashifi says they squandered life's capital in heedlessness and wasted their capacity for perfection by pursuing desires and following appetites.
BURSEVI:v6p77/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي (س كروه آنندكه زيان كرده اند ازنفسهاي

BURSEVI:v6p77/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p77/r5.claim: Al-Tawilat compares a person to an egg whose potential becomes a chick through the hen's care; once that potential is altered and care ends, it cannot be restored. A mystic who abandons the path is worse off than one abandoning the legal religion.
BURSEVI:v6p77/r5.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : الإنسان كالبيضة المستعدة لقبول تصرف ولاية الدجاجة

BURSEVI:v6p77/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p77/r6.claim: The altered spiritual nature explains remaining in Hell: the ruined potential cannot be brought back to its former state.
BURSEVI:v6p77/r6.anchor: أي في جهنم أنفسهم فلا يخرجون بالفروخية وليس من سنة الله إصلاح الاستعداد

BURSEVI:v6p77/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77/r7.speaker: الجامي
BURSEVI:v6p77/r7.claim: Jami's couplet says that one swallowed by the earth cannot be brought out even by Moses and Aaron, and no healer can repair the reversal of fate.
BURSEVI:v6p77/r7.anchor: قال الجامي : آنراكه زمين كشد درون ون قارون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r8.claim: The author calls the apposition analysis unusual: it means “settled in Hell,” a rhetorical apposition between equivalent referents because losing oneself leads to Hell; the apparent syntax makes Hell the predicate, not an adjective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r8.anchor: جعل في جهنم بدلا من خسروا وهذا بدل غريب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r1.claim: Light scales may mean scales of good deeds or deeds carrying no weight—evil deeds—depending on whether unbelievers’ deeds are weighed.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r1.anchor: أي موازين أعماله الحسنة أو أعماله التي لا وزن لها ولا اعتداد بها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r2.claim: Those who lose themselves waste the time to mature and destroy their capacity to attain perfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r2.anchor: ضيعوها بتضييع زمان استكمالها وأبطلو استعدادها لنيل كمالها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r3.claim: The demonstrative points to the group by meaning, while singular pronouns follow its grammatical form.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r3.anchor: واسم الإشارة في الموضعين عبارة عن الموصول وجمعه باعتبار معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r4.claim: ‘Abiding in Hell’ may be a second predicate or explanation; al-Zamakhsharī seems to prefer apposition to the relative clause, which al-Ālūsī rejects with Abū Ḥayyān’s objection that it is strange.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#3/r4.anchor: قال الخفاجي : أي بدل اشتمال لأن خلودهم في جهنم يشتمل على خسرانهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r2.claim: Those whose scales are light have lost themselves and remain in Hell.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r1.claim: Those with light scales are unbelievers; the Quran says God will assign them no weight on Resurrection Day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r1.anchor: وهم الكفار لقوله تعالى: { فلا نقيم لهم يوم القيمة وزنا }

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r2.claim: They lose themselves by wasting the time and capacity to attain perfection; their lasting place is Hell.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r2.anchor: غبنوها حيث ضيعوا زمان استكمالها وأبطلوا استعدادها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r6.claim: Those with light scales neglected faith-based deeds and lose themselves by following appetites in the abode of action; they remain forever in a Hell whose fire never dies out.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r6.anchor: باتباعها شهواتها في دار الأعمال وشغلها بأهوائها عن مراتب الكمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.claim: The main consequence concerns the weighed deeds, answering the rejected plea for return; the denial of kinship first cuts off hope of help or intercession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.anchor: والمقصود التفريع الثاني في قوله { فمن ثقلت موازينه } إلى آخره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r6.claim: Loss originally describes failed trade; here it depicts ruined hopes for idol intercession or escape from resurrection, as in 6:12 and 7:9.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r6.anchor: والخسارة : نقصان مال التجارة وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { الذين خسروا أنفسهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r7.claim: They lose themselves because they expected salvation but found its opposite after rejecting Islam, as if their own selves had perished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r7.anchor: وهي هنا تمثيل لحال خيبتهم فيما كانوا يأملونه من شفاعة أصنامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r8.claim: Anfusahum is the direct object of khasirū, while the demonstratives distinguish the two groups by their qualities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r8.anchor: ولذلك نصب { أنفسهم } على المفعول ب { خسروا } . واسما الإشارة لزيادة تمييز الفريقين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r1.claim: Mawazin is plural because the weighed things, the deeds, are plural; weighing makes the proof tangible in familiar human terms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r1.anchor: جمع «الموازين» من حيث الموزون جمع وهي الأعمال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r2.claim: A disbeliever's unbelief may be placed against an empty pan, or against good deeds such as charity to kin, which it outweighs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r2.anchor: إما أن يوضع كفره في كفة فلا يجد شيئا يعادله في الكفة الأخرى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r4.claim: Light scales mean bad deeds outweigh good deeds, leaving their owners failed, ruined, and bankrupt.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.claim: A report says an angel calls out the eternal felicity or misery of each person according to the balance's weight; Ibn Kathīr grades its chain weak because Dāwūd al-Muḥabbar is abandoned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.anchor: عن ثابت البناني وجعفر بن زيد ومنصور بن زاذان، عن أنس بن مالك يرفعه قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.claim: The damned are called lasting residents of Hell who do not depart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r6.anchor: أي: ماكثون، دائمون مقيمون لا يظعنون

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r9.claim: The ṣūr is a horn or a plural meaning images; lafh and nafh both mean striking the face, but lafh has a stronger effect.
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r9.anchor: الصور: كالقرن ينفخ فيه، والصور: جمع صورة. واللفح والنفح بمعنى واحد

SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r1.claim: خالدون may be a second predicate of أولئك or the predicate of an omitted subject هم.
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون " خالدون " خبرا ثانيا ل " أولئك "

SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats في جهنم خالدون as بدل from خسروا أنفسهم, with neither phrase having syntactic position because it is a relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: { في جهنم خالدون } بدل من

SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r3.claim: The Shaykh calls this an unusual بدل: only the phrase في جهنم replaces an implied استقروا, as the result of losing oneself is settlement in Hell.
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r3.anchor: جعل " في جهنم " بدلا من " خسروا " وهذا بدل غريب

SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r4.claim: The author says al-Zamakhshari's wording makes the entire خالدون phrase a بدل, not just في جهنم; the reported follow-up alternatives fit خالدون, while the Shaykh's account also leaves it stranded.
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r4.anchor: فجعل الشيخ الجار والمجرور البدل دون " خالدون " والزمخشري جعل جميع ذلك بدلا

SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows the relative clause to describe the demonstrative, but the author questions this because it is apparently its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:23:103/r5.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون الموصول نعتا لاسم الإشارة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r2.claim: “Abiding in Hell” may be an apposition to “they lost themselves,” a predicate after “those,” or a predicate with an omitted subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r2.anchor: في جهنم خالدون } بدل من خسروا أنفسهم ، ولا محل للبدل والمبدل منه ؛ لأن الصلة لا محل لها . أو خبر بعد خبر لأولئك

MUQATIL:23:101-105/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r3.claim: Unbelievers have light scales, lose themselves, and remain in Hell without dying.
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r3.anchor: خالدون } [آية: 103] لا يموتون { تلفح } يعنى تنفخ

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r1.claim: The light scales are weighed down by evil deeds; the intended people are unbelievers, who have cheated themselves and remain in Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ ومن خفت موازينه ﴾ بالسيئات والمراد الكفار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r2.claim: “Abiding” may parse as a substitute for “lost themselves,” as another predicate of “those,” or as the predicate of an omitted subject.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#3/r2.anchor: يدل من خسروا أنفسهم و محل للبدل والمبدل منه لأنه الصلة

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r2.claim: After the Trumpet comes accounting and the division between the blessed, whose scales are heavy, and the wretched, whose scales are light.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r2.anchor: أن بعد النفخ في الصور تكون المحاسبة

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r3.claim: Some infer that everyone must belong either to the saved or the damned, ruling out people with no entitlement to reward or punishment and those whose two are equal.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r3.anchor: وجب أن يكون كل مكلف لا بد وأن يكون من أهل الجنة وأهل الفلاح أو من أهل النار

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r4.claim: One interpretation treats the scales as a metaphor for justice.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r5.claim: A second takes the scales as good deeds: deeds with value win, while weightless deeds like a mirage leave their doer in Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r5.anchor: أن الموازين هي الأعمال الحسنة فمن أتي بما له قدر وخطر فهو الفائز الظافر

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the scales are plural of weighed things: righteous deeds valued by God; “no weight” means no worth.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما الموازين جمع موزون وهي الموزونات من الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r7.claim: A third interpretation is a real scale with a tongue and two pans, weighing good deeds in beautiful form and evil deeds in ugly form.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r7.anchor: أنه ميزان له لسان وكفتان يوزن فيه الحسنات

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains losing oneself as being cheated because the believers inherit the lost person's place.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما غبنوها بأن صارت منازلهم للمؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r9.claim: Another explanation is that the damned cannot benefit from themselves because they are trapped in punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r9.anchor: وقيل امتنع انتفاعهم بأنفسهم لكونهم في العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r10.claim: The wording that they abide in Hell plainly establishes the unbelievers' everlasting punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r10.anchor: ودلالته على خلود الكفار في النار بينة

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r11.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r11.claim: Al-Kashshaf analyzes “abiding in Hell” as an apposition, a second predicate of “those,” or a predicate with an omitted subject.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r11.anchor: بدل من خسروا أنفسهم أو خبر بعد خبر

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that the verse assigns punishment to bad deeds, which would be unjust if God created human acts.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r18.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : الآية تدل على أنهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.claim: Al-Razi answers that an unmotivated sin would be accidental, not voluntary, and so could not merit punishment; if motivated, its cause was not the person's act without an infinite regress, making the resulting act compelled and undeserving of reward.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r19.anchor: إن صدرت المعصية عنه لا لمرجح ألبتة كان صدورها عنه اتفاقيا لا اختياريا

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.anchor: will desire to go back to the world in order to do good instead of evil, though it will be too late for them (vv.99–118)

STUDYQURAN:23:102/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r1.claim: The commentary directs readers to its discussion of the scales of deeds at 101:6–9.
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r1.anchor: For a discussion of the scales of deeds, see 101:6–9c

STUDYQURAN:23:102/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r2.claim: The phrase 'lose their souls' may also be translated as 'lose themselves.'
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r2.anchor: Lose their souls could also be rendered “lose themselves.”

TAB-FULL:v17p115/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r1.claim: People whose good deeds weigh little and whose sins outweigh them have lost their share of God's mercy and remain in Hell.
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r1.anchor: موازين حسناته، فرجحت بها موازين سيئاته

TABRISI:23:101-108/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101-108/r10.claim: Those whose scales are light because of deficient obedience have lost themselves and remain in Hell; the mechanics of weighing were discussed under al-Aʿrāf.
TABRISI:23:101-108/r10.anchor: عن الطاعات { فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r2.claim: Those with light scales have ruined themselves by failing to gain, and they remain in Hell without leaving or dying.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r2.anchor: {ومن خفت موازينه فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم} [المؤمنون: 103] أن يغنموها فصاروا في النار.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.claim: Salvation depends on the amount of reward earned through faith and good works: those whose deeds weigh heavily succeed, while those whose scales are light suffer loss and enter enduring Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.anchor: tartıları yani sevapları ağır basanlar kurtuluşa erecek, tartıları hafif kalanlar da derin bir hüsrana uğrayacak, ebedî ve dehşetli bir azap sürecini yaşamak üzere cehenneme atılacaklardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r2.claim: The nature of grave life, barzakh, resurrection, and the scales lies beyond empirical and rational knowledge; believers should affirm them and prepare for the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r2.anchor: Mümine düşen, bunlara şeksiz şüphesiz inanıp gerektiği şekilde âhiret hazırlığı yapmaktır.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.claim: Only deeds will matter on Judgment Day; relationships will not avail anyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.anchor: On that day, only deeds – and not relationships – will be any avail.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r1.claim: Rhetoric scholars often express their ideas through hints, allusion, metonymy, and indirection, requiring readers to uncover the intended point through close thought.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r1.anchor: وجدت جله أو كله رمزا ووحيا وكناية وتعريضا وإيماء إلى الغرض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r2.claim: Readers repeat terms such as “verbal majesty,” “a special method,” and “a particular aspect” without explaining what merit those labels identify.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r2.anchor: ويقولون في المراد بالطريقة والوجه ما يحلى منه السامع بطائل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r3.claim: Descriptions like a word being firm, unsettled, well-cast, or cramped concern meaning and composition, not transient sounds that cannot literally remain fixed in a place.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p330/r3.anchor: والقلق في اللفظ محال فإنما يتمكن الشيء ويعلق إذا كان شيئا
